_meta.indication: MACRILEN is a growth hormone (GH) secretagogue receptor agonist indicated for the diagnosis of adult growth hormone deficiency (AGHD).

pivotal_trials.design: Multicenter, multinational, open-label, randomized, single dose, two-way crossover study comparing the macimorelin (MAC) growth hormone stimulation test to the insulin tolerance test (ITT); each subject served as their own control.
pivotal_trials.population: Adult subjects spanning high to low pre-test probability of adult growth hormone deficiency in four groups: Group A high likelihood (n=38), Group B intermediate likelihood (n=37), Group C low likelihood (n=40), Group D healthy control (n=25).
pivotal_trials.endpoint: Two co-primary endpoints: Percent Negative Agreement (benchmark 75%) and Percent Positive Agreement (benchmark 70%) between the macimorelin test and the insulin tolerance test.
pivotal_trials.n: 140 subjects in the modified intent-to-treat population (of 157 dosed; 74 ITT-positive, 66 ITT-negative).
pivotal_trials.result: Negative agreement 94% (95% CI 85%, 98%) met the 75% benchmark; positive agreement was 74% (95% CI 63%, 84%), with the lower bound 63% below the pre-specified 70% margin, so the positive-agreement co-primary endpoint was not met.

nct_ctgov.title: Validation of Macimorelin as a Test for Adult Growth Hormone Deficiency

key_safety: Most common adverse reactions were dysgeusia (4.5%), dizziness (3.9%), headache (3.9%), fatigue (3.9%), nausea (3.2%), hunger (3.2%), diarrhea, upper respiratory tract infection, feeling hot, hyperhidrosis, nasopharyngitis, and sinus bradycardia. A key safety concern is QT prolongation (about 11 msec increase in QTc), which can lead to torsade de pointes-type ventricular tachycardia.
target_moa: Macimorelin is a synthetic growth hormone secretagogue receptor agonist (ghrelin receptor agonist) that stimulates GH release by activating growth hormone secretagogue receptors in the pituitary and hypothalamus.
modality: Small molecule (synthetic peptidomimetic ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor agonist).

advisory_committee.vote: No advisory committee was convened; the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues requiring outside expertise.

orphan_indication.text: Macimorelin received orphan drug designation from the Office of Orphan Products Development for the diagnosis of adult GHD on September 25, 2009 (designation request number 06-2255).

summary.text: Macrilen (macimorelin) is a 505(b)(1) NDA for a ghrelin/growth hormone secretagogue receptor agonist with orphan drug designation for the diagnosis of adult growth hormone deficiency. The original NDA (submitted November 4, 2014) received a Complete Response Letter dated 11/05/2014; the applicant conducted a new confirmatory trial (AEZS-130-052) and a thorough QT study, and the priority resubmission (received June 30, 2017) was approved without an advisory committee.

citations.quote: On November 4, 2014 Aeterna-Zentaris submitted a New Drug Application (NDA) for Macrilen under section 505(b)(1) of the Food, Drug and Cosmetic Act.
The drug received orphan designation status (Orphan Designation# 06-2255) for this indication.

To address the deficiencies the applicant was asked to establish the efficacy of Macrilen in a new confirmatory clinical trial and to conduct a dedicated thorough QT study to characterize the effect of macimorelin on cardiac repolarization.

Your application for macimorelin was not referred to an FDA advisory committee because the clinical trial design was acceptable, the application did not raise significant safety or efficacy issues that were unexpected in the intended population and the application did not raise significant public health questions on the role of the drug in the diagnosis, cure, mitigation, treatment, or prevention of a disease.
1 For full details refer to Complete Response Letter in DARRTS dated 11/05/14 (Reference ID: 3653987)

basis.text: The applicant had not provided sufficient evidence that the Macrilen stimulation test can accurately diagnose growth hormone deficiency in adults; the primary analysis failed to demonstrate accuracy of the test.

citations.quote: I agree with recommendations made by Drs. Lubas and Roman and recommend a complete response because the applicant has not provided sufficient evidence that the Macrilen stimulation test can accurately diagnose growth hormone deficiency in adults.
